unit.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: Two rigid bodies have the same moment of inertia about their axes of symmetry. Which body will have the greater kinetic energy?

verification.note: TSBIE Basic Learning Material (2021-22), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER — this question is NOT in the Sri Chaitanya Fastrack; the two source books are not supersets of each other, so the unit inventory is their union. The 1+1 split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The relation
lines: Rotational kinetic energy in terms of
steps.margin_note: This is the rotational twin of KE = p²/2m from Work Power Energy — same substitution, ω = L/I.
steps.why: KE = ½Iω² and L = Iω; putting ω = L/I into the first gives KE = L²/2I. Knowing both forms lets you answer with whichever quantity the question fixes.
common_mistakes: Using KE = ½Iω² and getting stuck, because the question says nothing about ω.

accept: KE is L squared by two I
reject: the body with greater angular momentum

steps.label: The answer
lines: With I the same for both bodies,

lines.text: the body with the greater angular
momentum has the greater kinetic energy.

steps.margin_note: State the condition ("I same for both") before the conclusion — it is what makes the comparison fair.
steps.why: The question deliberately fixes I so that L alone decides. The same trick with p²/2m appeared on both boards’ papers — learn the pattern, not just this case.
common_mistakes: Answering "the faster one" — ω is not given; the comparison the formula allows is through L.

recall.must_convey: That with equal I, the body with greater angular momentum has greater kinetic energy.
accept: the body with greater angular momentum
